name: RUCKUS ICX Layer 2 Switch Security Technical Implementation Guide
description: This Security Technical Implementation Guide is published as a tool to improve the security of Department of Defense (DOD) information systems. The requirements are derived from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-53 and related documents. Comments or proposed revisions to this document should be sent via email to the following address: disa.stig_spt@mail.mil.

rules.title: The RUCKUS ICX switch must be configured to disable nonessential capabilities.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must uniquely identify all network-connected endpoint devices before establishing any connection.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must disable the Multiple VLAN Registration Protocol (MVRP).
The RUCKUS ICX switch must manage excess bandwidth to limit the effects of packet flooding types of denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must authenticate all network-connected endpoint devices before establishing any connection.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have Root Protect enabled on all switch ports connecting to access layer switches and hosts.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have Bridge Protocol Data Unit (BPDU) Guard enabled on all user-facing or untrusted access switch ports.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) Loop Detect enabled on all nondesignated STP switch ports
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have Unknown Unicast Flood Blocking (UUFB) enabled.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have DHCP snooping for all user VLANs to validate DHCP messages from untrusted sources.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have IP Source Guard enabled on all user-facing or untrusted access switch ports.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have Dynamic Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) Inspection (DAI) enabled on all user VLANs.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have Storm Control configured on all host-facing switch ports.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have IGMP or MLD Snooping configured on all VLANs.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must implement Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) where VLANs span multiple switches with redundant links.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must enable Unidirectional Link Detection (UDLD) to protect against one-way connections.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have all disabled switch ports assigned to an unused VLAN.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must not have the default VLAN assigned to any host-facing switch ports.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have the default VLAN pruned from all trunk ports that do not require it.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must not use the default VLAN for management traffic.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must have all user-facing or untrusted ports configured as access switch ports.
The RUCKUS ICX layer 2 switch must have the native VLAN assigned to an ID other than the default VLAN for all 802.1q trunk links.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must not have any switch ports assigned to the native VLAN.
The RUCKUS ICX switch must implement physically or logically separate subnetworks to isolate organization-defined critical system components and functions.
